pdf: D:\CLAUDE\Projet CFA\CFA L1\6. TOUGH QB UWORLD-2000 MCQs\10. Ethics\11.04 Introduction To The Global Investment Performance Standards (GIPS) - Answers.pdf
subtopic: 11.04 Introduction To The Global Investment Performance Standards (GIPS)
question_en: An investment firm has multiple subsidiaries across countries. The subsidiaries have different business names but operate under the same brand name. When defining the firm to claim compliance with GIPS standards, which subsidiaries should the firm most appropriately include?
option_a: Any subsidiaries operating under the same brand name
option_b: Only subsidiaries using the business name of the investment firm
option_c: Only subsidiaries located in the country the firm is seeking compliance
explanation_en: The fundamentals of compliance require that a company seeking compliance with GIPS standards must properly define its firm. A proper definition ensures: the whole firm is complying with GIPS standards, an accurate accounting of total firm assets, and representative composite creation. GIPS standards state that an investment firm seeking compliance should adopt the broadest definition of the firm. When a company operates in multiple countries or regions, the scope should include all subsidiaries or offices that operate under the same brand name. This includes any individual subsidiaries that may have different business names. For example, if a company has a subsidiary in another country with a different business name but that operates under the same brand name, it should be included under the definition of the firm for GIPS compliance. (Choice B) The definition of the firm should include all geographical subsidiaries operating under the same brand name, regardless of the actual names of the individual companies. (Choice C) GIPS compliance encompasses the whole firm and is not done on a country-by-country basis.

pdf: D:\CLAUDE\Projet CFA\CFA L1\6. TOUGH QB UWORLD-2000 MCQs\10. Ethics\11.04 Introduction To The Global Investment Performance Standards (GIPS) - Answers.pdf
subtopic: 11.04 Introduction To The Global Investment Performance Standards (GIPS)
question_en: When constructing a composite, which of the following is least likely a requirement of GIPS?
option_a: Each composite must include two or more discretionary portfolios.
option_b: A portfolio's inclusion in a composite is determined on an ex ante basis.
option_c: All actual, fee-paying, discretionary portfolios are required to be in at least one composite.
explanation_en: A composite is an aggregated portfolio formed by grouping one or more portfolios that a firm manages according to a specific style or objective. Firms report the portfolios' combined performance as if it were one collective unit. Most composites are constructed using many portfolios. However, a composite can consist of only one portfolio if the style or objective is unique to that portfolio. To be GIPS-compliant, a firm must include all actual, discretionary, fee-paying, portfolios in at least one composite (Choice C). Hypothetical portfolios cannot be included since composites must represent actual results. The term "discretionary" indicates that the client has given the manager control to make investment decisions (ie, buy or sell securities). Including only the portfolios that the manager controls provides the best evidence of the manager's skill. (Choice B) The decision whether to include a portfolio in a composite must be made prior to the reporting period; this is referred to as ex ante, rather than ex post. This prevents managers from "cherry picking" or selecting only those portfolios that boost the composite's performance.

pdf: D:\CLAUDE\Projet CFA\CFA L1\6. TOUGH QB UWORLD-2000 MCQs\10. Ethics\11.04 Introduction To The Global Investment Performance Standards (GIPS) - Answers.pdf
subtopic: 11.04 Introduction To The Global Investment Performance Standards (GIPS)
question_en: An investment management firm most likely can claim compliance with the Global Investment Performance Standards (GIPS) if it:
option_a: includes only discretionary portfolios in its composites.
option_b: clearly distinguishes composites that do and do not comply with GIPS.
option_c: excludes composites for which it has less than five years of performance history.
explanation_en: Compliance with the Global Investment Performance Standards (GIPS) requires firms to calculate and present composite returns. A composite is a group of discretionary portfolios that a firm manages according to a common style or strategy. A discretionary portfolio is one in which the manager makes the investment decisions. For example, a firm's large-cap value composite would consist of the portfolios that have a strategy that invests in large-cap value stocks. A firm must present a composite for each of its different strategies, but nondiscretionary portfolios are not included in a composite. (Choice B) GIPS are a set of detailed provisions and definitions concerning input data, calculation, composite construction, and so on. For a firm to claim compliance, all composites must be prepared according to GIPS; the Standards specifically disallow firms to claim compliance "except for" noncompliant composites. (Choice C) GIPS generally require firms to present a minimum of five years of returns for each composite. However, with respect to newer composites, a firm complies with GIPS if it presents information for each year of a composite's existence. Even if a composite has existed for less than five years, it must be included for a firm to claim compliance with GIPS.

pdf: D:\CLAUDE\Projet CFA\CFA L1\6. TOUGH QB UWORLD-2000 MCQs\10. Ethics\11.04 Introduction To The Global Investment Performance Standards (GIPS) - Answers.pdf
subtopic: 11.04 Introduction To The Global Investment Performance Standards (GIPS)
question_en: A firm creating and maintaining GIPS-compliant composites is most likely required to:
option_a: assign portfolios to composites on an ex ante basis.
option_b: ensure that each composite contains multiple portfolios.
option_c: include every portfolio with a similar strategy in a composite.
explanation_en: A composite aggregates all a firm's portfolios that are managed according to a certain investment mandate, objective, or strategy. GIPS require that each fee-paying, discretionary portfolio must be included in at least one composite. The decision to include a portfolio in a composite must be based on pre-established criteria, referred to as ex ante, rather than ex post (ie, after the fact), criteria. This prevents managers from presenting only their best-performing portfolios in the composite. Including all similarly managed portfolios provides a complete representation of the firm's performance with that strategy. (Choice B) Including only one portfolio in a composite is allowed if it is the firm's only portfolio using that investment mandate, objective, or strategy. (Choice C) A firm is required only to include fee-paying, discretionary portfolios in composites. Non–fee-paying portfolios that are discretionary also may be included. However, all nondiscretionary portfolios must be excluded since they reflect clients', not the firm's, decisions and performance.

pdf: D:\CLAUDE\Projet CFA\CFA L1\6. TOUGH QB UWORLD-2000 MCQs\10. Ethics\11.04 Introduction To The Global Investment Performance Standards (GIPS) - Answers.pdf
subtopic: 11.04 Introduction To The Global Investment Performance Standards (GIPS)
question_en: The fundamental purpose of the GIPS standards for firms is best described as:
option_a: fully, fairly, and ethically presenting a firm's investment performance.
option_b: serving as the global regulatory source to address controversial performance reporting.
option_c: setting a minimum threshold for composite performance reporting, verified by a third party.
explanation_en: Global Investment Performance Standards (GIPS®) are a standardized approach for investment performance presentation. GIPS standards are based on the ethical principle that fair representation and full disclosure of investment performance are critical to the integrity of the capital markets and the investment profession. For firms, the fundamental purpose of GIPS compliance is to present investment performance fully, fairly, and ethically. (Choice B) CFA Institute is not a regulatory body. GIPS standards are a self-regulatory set of standards that lays out a framework for global performance reporting without attempting to address every element (controversial or not) of performance reporting practices. (Choice C) The GIPS standards set a much higher bar than a minimum threshold for composite performance reporting. In addition, third-party verification is optional, although it is considered best practice.

pdf: D:\CLAUDE\Projet CFA\CFA L1\6. TOUGH QB UWORLD-2000 MCQs\10. Ethics\11.04 Introduction To The Global Investment Performance Standards (GIPS) - Answers.pdf
subtopic: 11.04 Introduction To The Global Investment Performance Standards (GIPS)
question_en: For Global Investment Performance Standards (GIPS®) compliant firms, which of the following best describes the purpose of composite construction?
option_a: Equal trade allocations ensure consistent reporting.
option_b: Composites' universal asset class definitions improve comparability.
option_c: Composites bar managers from preparing performance reports using only the best accounts.
explanation_en: GIPS standards provide rules on how a manager must construct and report composites. A composite is made up of one or more client portfolios that represent a firm's strategy. Each portfolio may be included in one or more composites. The purpose of having uniformity in constructing composites is to prevent firms from selecting accounts that make the firm's performance look better than it would if all appropriate accounts were included. Without GIPS standards, a firm could choose which portfolios to include and exclude, making it difficult to ascertain how managers truly perform. GIPS-compliant firms produce performance reports that are more consistent and reliable. (Choice A) GIPS standards do not require managers to allocate trades equally. The Standard of Professional Conduct stipulates that clients should be fairly treated, but it is silent on an exact process for allocating trades. (Choice B) GIPS standards do not mandate universal asset class definitions in composites.

pdf: D:\CLAUDE\Projet CFA\CFA L1\6. TOUGH QB UWORLD-2000 MCQs\10. Ethics\11.04 Introduction To The Global Investment Performance Standards (GIPS) - Answers.pdf
subtopic: 11.04 Introduction To The Global Investment Performance Standards (GIPS)
question_en: If a firm chooses to verify its compliance with the GIPS standards, the verification must be performed by:
option_a: an independent third party.
option_b: the firm's chief compliance officer.
option_c: the local securities market regulatory authority.
explanation_en: GIPS verification Is recommended but not required Must be performed by an independent third party Applies to the entire firm, not just specific composites Increases confidence in a firm's claim of GIPS compliance Compliance with GIPS (Global Investment Performance Standards) is voluntary, but a firm must fully comply to claim compliance; there is no partial compliance. For the firm that claims compliance, CFA Institute recommends (but does not require) that compliance be verified to enhance the reliability of the firm's assertion. Verification must be made by an independent third party and is applied to an entire firm, not individual composites. Verification does not ensure the accuracy of the composites but tests whether the firm: has complied with all GIPS requirements when constructing its composites and follows a process for calculating and presenting performance returns that complies with GIPS. (Choice B) A firm can assert that it is GIPS compliant, but it cannot self-verify its assertion. A firm's chief compliance officer, or any other person who is part of the firm, is not allowed to perform the verification. (Choice C) Regulatory bodies are not involved in verifying GIPS compliance.

pdf: D:\CLAUDE\Projet CFA\CFA L1\6. TOUGH QB UWORLD-2000 MCQs\10. Ethics\11.04 Introduction To The Global Investment Performance Standards (GIPS) - Answers.pdf
subtopic: 11.04 Introduction To The Global Investment Performance Standards (GIPS)
question_en: Which of the following most accurately describes a reason why the Global Investment Performance Standards were developed?
option_a: To encourage diversity in performance reporting
option_b: To set a minimum period for reporting past performance
option_c: To provide flexibility in how terminated accounts are reported
explanation_en: The Global Investment Performance Standards (GIPS) are a uniform approach for calculating and presenting historical investment performance. With fair representation and full disclosure, all interested parties benefit from more reliable data. Prior to the development of GIPS, investors had difficulty comparing managers since there was a wide disparity in how managers calculated and presented performance information. Intitially, for GIPS-compliant firms, performance reports must show at least five years of performance unless the firm or composite has existed for less than five years. In this case, firms present performance since the firm's or composite's inception. In subsequent years, the firm must add GIPS-compliant performance each year until there is a minimum of 10 years of performance in the firm's reports. (Choice A) GIPS provide uniformity, not diversity when presenting performance. Uniformity gives the investor the ability to compare managers who use the same method to calculate performance. (Choice C) GIPS require managers to include terminated client accounts as part of the firm's historical performance. Excluding underperforming portfolios that were terminated may overstate performance and so would be an unfair representation. There is no flexibility on how to account for terminated portfolios.

pdf: D:\CLAUDE\Projet CFA\CFA L1\6. TOUGH QB UWORLD-2000 MCQs\10. Ethics\11.04 Introduction To The Global Investment Performance Standards (GIPS) - Answers.pdf
subtopic: 11.04 Introduction To The Global Investment Performance Standards (GIPS)
question_en: Parkhurst Investment Advisors (PIA) is a fee-based provider of stock selection and asset allocation advice to large, defined-benefit pension plans. It does not manage assets but maintains detailed records on its recommendations. For the last 12 years, PIA has created composites from the different portfolios that it has recommended to its clients. In its advertising literature, PIA displays each year's return for its composites, both gross of and net of a hypothetical 1% annual fee, as well as the return for each composite's benchmark. Can PIA claim compliance with the Global Investment Performance Standards (GIPS)?
option_a: No, since it does not manage assets.
option_b: No, since GIPS place a 10-year limit on past information.
option_c: Yes, since it presents the returns for the composites as well as their benchmarks.
explanation_en: Global Investment Performance Standards (GIPS) provide uniform methods for investment managers to calculate and present investment results. Using GIPS to calculate and present performance allows the investing public to objectively compare different managers. It prevents firms from presenting information for a limited time horizon that may not represent the longer-term reality. Although compliance is voluntary, one condition to claim compliance with GIPS is that a firm must manage assets. Advisers and software developers that aid asset managers cannot claim compliance since they do not actually manage client assets. In this case, although PIA can demonstrate the returns that its portfolios would have achieved, it is not allowed to claim compliance with GIPS. (Choice B) GIPS requires a firm to present at least five years of returns for each of the composite portfolios that it manages. A "composite" portfolio is one that is aggregated from one or more actual portfolios that the firm manages according to a distinct style or objective. GIPS does not limit the number of years of information that can be provided. (Choice C) A firm must present information concerning both its composites and their benchmarks. However, since PIA does not manage assets, it cannot claim to be GIPS-compliant.

pdf: D:\CLAUDE\Projet CFA\CFA L1\6. TOUGH QB UWORLD-2000 MCQs\10. Ethics\11.04 Introduction To The Global Investment Performance Standards (GIPS) - Answers.pdf
subtopic: 11.04 Introduction To The Global Investment Performance Standards (GIPS)
question_en: If an investment firm has its GIPS compliance verified, the verifier must attest that the firm is compliant at the:
option_a: firm level.
option_b: account level.
option_c: composite level.
explanation_en: According to the Fundamentals of Compliance provision of the GIPS, to claim compliance a firm must adhere to all GIPS requirements. This is accomplished only if the entire firm follows all mandated rules. Firms that claim GIPS compliance enhance potential clients' confidence that the information used is complete and fairly presented. If the Standards are not applied on a firm-wide basis, managers could include only those portfolios that present the firm in the best light (ie, cherry-pick accounts), which could mislead investors. (Choice B) Composites are groups of accounts managed in a similar strategy, all of which must, without exception, comply with GIPS for a firm to claim GIPS compliance. (Choice C) Account performance data must be appropriately maintained and may be part of a composite. However, the basis of claiming GIPS compliance is at the firm level, not the account level.

pdf: D:\CLAUDE\Projet CFA\CFA L1\6. TOUGH QB UWORLD-2000 MCQs\10. Ethics\11.04 Introduction To The Global Investment Performance Standards (GIPS) - Answers.pdf
subtopic: 11.04 Introduction To The Global Investment Performance Standards (GIPS)
question_en: A firm is in a jurisdiction where local regulations concerning investment reporting requirements are very similar to the Global Investment Performance Standards (GIPS), except that a firm cannot provide performance information for composites that are in existence for less than five years. If the firm follows local regulations, can it claim that it is GIPS-compliant?
option_a: No, since a firm must comply with all the Standards to claim GIPS-compliance.
option_b: Yes, provided that the firm indicates where GIPS conflicts with local regulations.
option_c: Yes, provided that the firm furnishes independent verification that it follows local regulations.
explanation_en: Global Investment Performance Standards (GIPS) require firms to include five years of performance information for all composites. If a composite has been in existence for less than five years, then the information must be provided from the composite's inception. In this question, GIPS conflict with local law, since firms are not permitted under local law to report on composites that have been in existence for less than five years. The general rule is that a firm must comply with all Standards to claim it is GIPS-compliant. However, the Standards also require firms to comply with local law. GIPS are intended to apply globally, so when GIPS conflict with local law, a firm can claim compliance with GIPS by following local law and disclosing those areas where GIPS conflict (Choice A). (Choice C) The CFA Institute recommends, but does not require, that firms verify their compliance with GIPS. If a firm chooses to verify, the verification must be performed by an independent third party. Nothing in GIPS requires a firm to verify that it complies with local regulations in order to claim that it complies with GIPS.

pdf: D:\CLAUDE\Projet CFA\CFA L1\6. TOUGH QB UWORLD-2000 MCQs\10. Ethics\11.04 Introduction To The Global Investment Performance Standards (GIPS) - Answers.pdf
subtopic: 11.04 Introduction To The Global Investment Performance Standards (GIPS)
question_en: According to CFA Institute, which of the following are most likely to be the main beneficiaries of GIPS-compliant reporting?
option_a: Investment firms and prospective clients
option_b: Governmental regulators and investment firms
option_c: Prospective clients and governmental regulators
explanation_en: While it may be that market participants and society at large benefit from GIPS compliance, according to CFA Institute, both investment firms and potential clients are the main beneficiaries. GIPS-compliant firms benefit directly by increasing the integrity of their performance reporting with complete and fairly presented reports. Prospective clients benefit from increased confidence in the reliability of firms' performance. They also benefit from easier comparisons when selecting among investment firms. Complying with GIPS enhances firms' credibility but does not replace a potential investor's due diligence. (Choices B and C) Governmental regulators may have their own standards but do not directly benefit from GIPS-compliant firms.

pdf: D:\CLAUDE\Projet CFA\CFA L1\6. TOUGH QB UWORLD-2000 MCQs\10. Ethics\11.04 Introduction To The Global Investment Performance Standards (GIPS) - Answers.pdf
subtopic: 11.04 Introduction To The Global Investment Performance Standards (GIPS)
question_en: If a firm elects to verify its compliance with the Global Investment Performance Standards (GIPS), verification most likely:
option_a: is required at least annually.
option_b: must be performed on all the firm's composites.
option_c: ensures that a composite is accurately presented.
explanation_en: The Global Investment Performance Standards (GIPS) provide uniform methods for investment managers to calculate and present investment results. Compliance with GIPS is voluntary, but firms must comply with all the Standards to claim compliance; there is no partial compliance. When a firm claims that it complies with GIPS, CFA Institute recommends, but does not require, that the claim be verified. If elected, verification must be made by an independent third party. Verification is performed on all the firm's composites and tests two conditions: The firm has constructed its composites in accordance with GIPS. The firm's process for calculating and presenting performance returns complies with GIPS. (Choice A) CFA Institute recommends that firms verify their claims of compliance with GIPS, but it is not required. (Choice C) Verification only tests that the firm followed GIPS in constructing its composites. It does not ensure that a composite is accurately presented.

pdf: D:\CLAUDE\Projet CFA\CFA L1\6. TOUGH QB UWORLD-2000 MCQs\10. Ethics\11.04 Introduction To The Global Investment Performance Standards (GIPS) - Answers.pdf
subtopic: 11.04 Introduction To The Global Investment Performance Standards (GIPS)
question_en: Firm X acquires Firm Y. Both firms have historically claimed GIPS compliance. In the acquisition, all of Firm Y's portfolio managers have been retained by Firm X but most of the research and support staff have not. The research duties will be assumed by Firm X's existing staff. According to the GIPS standards, can Firm X link Firm Y's past performance with its own?
option_a: No.
option_b: Yes, since Firm X has acquired Firm Y.
option_c: Yes, since the portfolios' management remains the same.
explanation_en: Global Investment Performance Standards (GIPS®) are a standardized approach for investment performance presentation. GIPS compliance is on a firm-wide basis only (ie, not on a composite and/or fund level). When a new firm is created or an existing firm is acquired, the prior or existing firm's historical GIPS-compliant performance can be linked to (ie, assumed by and reported with) the new or acquiring firm's reported performance, provided that all of the following conditions are met: Substantially all the investment decision makers are employed by the new or acquiring firm. This includes not only portfolio managers but also the relevant research and support staff. The investment decision-making process must remain independent (ie, no interference by acquiring firm) and substantially intact. The new or acquiring firm must maintain records that support the reported performance. There is no break (ie, gap) in the performance record when transitioning to the new firm. If there is a break, the past performance can still be presented but not linked. In this scenario, since Firm X has not retained Firm Y's key investment decision-making personnel, Firm X cannot link Firm Y's past performance with its own (Choices B and C).

pdf: D:\CLAUDE\Projet CFA\CFA L1\6. TOUGH QB UWORLD-2000 MCQs\10. Ethics\11.04 Introduction To The Global Investment Performance Standards (GIPS) - Answers.pdf
subtopic: 11.04 Introduction To The Global Investment Performance Standards (GIPS)
question_en: The GIPS standards most likely:
option_a: allow selection of the period to be presented for a composite and its benchmark.
option_b: require inclusion of portfolios removed from a composite after the reported period.
option_c: are enforced by regulatory authorities to ensure consistency among investment firms.
explanation_en: Common misleading performance reporting practices Representative Selecting top-performing portfolios to represent overall results accounts Survivorship Excluding terminated portfolios from average performance bias Varying Presenting only selected periods of strong performance time periods The Global Investment Performance Standards (GIPS®) standardize the reporting of historical performance across the investment industry to facilitate comparisons between firms and increase investor confidence. The GIPS standards require that information is comprehensive and represents actual performance. Investment managers at noncompliant firms could mislead clients by selectively choosing to present information on: Portfolios managed: A firm might choose to share the historical performance of its top-performing portfolios only, thus reporting greater returns than the actual results. Financial assets: A firm might present the investment performance of only currently invested assets, which creates survivorship bias by overlooking assets that were removed from the portfolio after performing poorly. Firms should include terminated client accounts, funds, and portfolios as part of the historical performance of a composite. Time period: Investment managers might inappropriately present the performance only for periods when a portfolio outperformed the market or the benchmark. (Choice A) The GIPS standards prevent firms from presenting performance periods selectively by mandating a minimum number of consecutive periods to present. (Choice C) GIPS compliance is optional, so there is no regulatory oversight of the GIPS standards.

pdf: D:\CLAUDE\Projet CFA\CFA L1\6. TOUGH QB UWORLD-2000 MCQs\10. Ethics\11.04 Introduction To The Global Investment Performance Standards (GIPS) - Answers.pdf
subtopic: 11.04 Introduction To The Global Investment Performance Standards (GIPS)
question_en: Based on the GIPS fundamentals of compliance, a firm must define:
option_a: the firm and discretion.
option_b: prospective clients and the firm.
option_c: discretion and prospective clients.
explanation_en: A firm seeking compliance with GIPS standards must define the firm and the meaning of discretion to ensure accuracy and consistency when applying the standards. GIPS standards state that an investment firm seeking compliance should adopt the broadest definition of the firm to ensure an accurate accounting of total firm assets. When a firm operates in multiple countries/regions, the scope of the definition of the firm should include all offices that operate under the same brand name. Firms must also define discretion so that they can be consistent about which portfolios will be included in composites. Since only discretionary portfolios are included in composites, this definition will dictate when a portfolio is included or removed from composites, which in turn affects reported performance. (Choices B and C) Firms claiming GIPS compliance do not consider a definition for prospective clients. Based on the fundamentals of compliance, firms must provide GIPS reports to all prospective clients and prospective pooled fund investors.

pdf: D:\CLAUDE\Projet CFA\CFA L1\6. TOUGH QB UWORLD-2000 MCQs\10. Ethics\11.04 Introduction To The Global Investment Performance Standards (GIPS) - Answers.pdf
subtopic: 11.04 Introduction To The Global Investment Performance Standards (GIPS)
question_en: To claim compliance with Global Investment Performance Standards (GIPS), a firm most likely will state that it:
option_a: calculates performance in accordance with GIPS.
option_b: includes portfolios in composites based on ex ante criteria.
option_c: omits reporting on composites that have been in existence for fewer than 5 years.
explanation_en: Global Investment Performance Standards®, known as GIPS, were created by CFA Institute to provide uniform methods for investment managers to calculate and present investment results. Compliance with GIPS is voluntary, but to claim compliance, a firm must comply with all of the standards; there is no partial compliance. A composite is an aggregation of portfolios that are managed to a specific style or strategy. One compliance requirement is that a firm generally must include all discretionary, fee-paying portfolios in a composite. However, if the firm has established specific criteria for including portfolios before creating the composite (ie, ex ante criteria), then it can still claim compliance with GIPS despite the exclusion of portfolios that do not comply with criteria. This prevents a firm from changing its rules to justify excluding one or more portfolios with subpar performance so that the overall results look better. (Choice A) CFA Institute specifically prohibits firms from using any language to the effect that they calculate returns in accordance with GIPS. (Choice C) Firms must present information on all composites for at least 5 years or since inception if the composite has existed for fewer than 5 years .

pdf: D:\CLAUDE\Projet CFA\CFA L1\6. TOUGH QB UWORLD-2000 MCQs\10. Ethics\11.04 Introduction To The Global Investment Performance Standards (GIPS) - Answers.pdf
subtopic: 11.04 Introduction To The Global Investment Performance Standards (GIPS)
question_en: GIPS standards prevent firms from using misleading performance measurement practices such as presenting:
option_a: average returns that exclude terminated portfolios.
option_b: fewer periods of returns than exist for an investment strategy.
option_c: returns of investment strategies that consist of a single portfolio.
explanation_en: Common misleading performance reporting practices Representative Selecting top-performing portfolios to represent overall results accounts Survivorship Excluding terminated portfolios from average performance bias Varying Presenting only selected periods of strong performance time periods The global standard for investment performance reporting known as GIPS (Global Investment Performance Standards) provides a uniform approach for calculating and presenting historical investment performance. Without the GIPS standards, a firm's reporting of its investment performance may be unreliable due to: selectively presenting top-performing portfolios to represent the firm's results for a given strategy, excluding portfolios that performed poorly and were terminated, or presenting returns for a period of strong performance while excluding periods of weaker performance. GIPS require that firms include terminated client accounts, funds, and portfolios as part of the historical performance of a composite. This practice results in a more accurate representation of a firm's complete performance. Excluding terminated portfolios that underperformed results in overstating performance and leads to misleading reporting. (Choice B) GIPS standards prevent firms from selectively presenting performance periods by mandating a minimum number of consecutive years to present. If the strategy has existed for more than the minimum number of required reporting years, firms are allowed to present fewer periods of historical performance than exist. (Choice C) Firms can present results of a single portfolio if it is the only one for a given strategy.

pdf: D:\CLAUDE\Projet CFA\CFA L1\6. TOUGH QB UWORLD-2000 MCQs\10. Ethics\11.05 Ethics Application - Answers.pdf
subtopic: 11.05 Ethics Application
question_en: Aditi Kumar is a Level II Candidate and a performance measurement and attribution analyst for an investment manager. On a quarterly basis, Kumar produces performance reports that include the firm's composites for each investment strategy. Raheem Khan, CFA, the portfolio manager of the firm's large-cap equity strategy approaches Kumar regarding the large-cap equity composite for the most recent quarter. Kumar explains that several accounts in the composite should be excluded from this quarter's performance report due to a software issue that resulted in numerous accounts not being fully invested. The resulting cash drag caused the composite to underperform the benchmark index for the quarter and year. Khan explains that he should not be held responsible for a software error. Kumar agrees and produces new reports without the affected accounts. According to Standard I(C) Misrepresentation, it is most likely that:
option_a: no violation occurred.
option_b: only Kumar violated the Standard.
option_c: both Kumar and Khan violated the Standard.
explanation_en: "Members and Candidates must:
